title: 2007 HMMT February Combinatorics Problem 1
statement: A committee of 5 is to be chosen from a group of 9 people. How many ways can it be chosen, if Biff and Jacob must serve together or not at all, and Alice and Jane refuse to serve with each other?

solutions.text: 41. If Biff and Jacob are on the committee, there are \(\binom{7}{3}=35\) ways for the other members to be chosen. Amongst these 35 possibilities, we reject the \(\binom{5}{1}=5\) choices where both Alice and Jane are also serving. If Biff and Jacob are not serving, then there are \(\binom{7}{5}=21\) ways to choose the remaining 5 members. Again, we reject the \(\binom{5}{3}=10\) instances where Alice and Jane are chosen, so the total is \((35-5)+(21-10)=41\).
